sources.entry: url-to-md - Any URL to clean markdown for LLMs. Free API, no signup required. Strips JS/CSS and outputs LLM-ready content.

summary.one_liner: url2md converts any web URL into clean, LLM-ready markdown by stripping ads, navigation, and boilerplate, with a web UI, a no-key API, and a local Python/Docker setup.
summary.what_it_does: Fetches a given URL with a clean user-agent, runs readability extraction (the algorithm Firefox Reader View uses), converts the resulting HTML to markdown with html2text, removes empty elements, and collapses whitespace. The response includes the page title, the markdown body, character count, a rough token estimate (chars divided by 4), line count, and a truncated flag. It can be used through a web page where you paste a URL, through a GET or POST API endpoint, or run locally with Python or Docker. The README states there are no accounts or tracking, and the API needs no key.
use_cases: paste web documentation into an AI coding assistant
convert a blog post or article to markdown for an LLM prompt
extract readable content from a URL without ads or navigation
estimate token count of a web page before sending it to a model
fetch page content programmatically via a simple HTTP API
notable: Uses readability extraction (same algorithm as Firefox Reader View) before markdown conversion
Returns a token count estimate and line/char counts alongside the markdown
No API key or signup required for the hosted API
Simple GET or POST JSON API
caveats: Hosted API is rate-limited to 30 requests per hour per IP
Token count is a rough estimate (characters divided by 4), not a real tokenizer count
README does not describe handling of JavaScript-rendered pages or paywalled content
